instructions.task: A buyer and a seller chatted to negotiate the price of a Craigslist item. After the chat the buyer could submit a formal offer that the seller accepts or rejects. Read the whole conversation, paying most attention to how it ends, and decide which pattern best describes how the negotiation ended.
rules: If both sides accepted the same price, it is an agreement, even if pickup, delivery, paperwork, an application or submitting the formal offer still remains.

If prices went back and forth (at least one offer and one counter-offer) and the chat simply stops on the latest proposal without a reply or a refusal, choose the unanswered counter pattern: the gap was narrowing and the formal offer likely settled it.
If the only price ever proposed is the buyer's first offer (or no counter was made) and the chat stops there, choose the unanswered opening offer pattern.
Choose walked away only when someone explicitly refuses the last offer, says they cannot agree, or leaves.
A chat where the parties were confused about the item or roles counts as broken only if the confusion was never resolved; if they sorted it out and reached agreement, it is an agreement.

criteria.mutual_agreement: Both parties clearly agreed on the same price and terms; the conversation ends with the deal accepted, possibly followed by logistics or thanks.
criteria.agreement_to_finalize_later: They agreed on a price, and only paperwork, an application, a viewing, payment or submitting the formal offer remains.
criteria.unanswered_counter: After real back-and-forth haggling (offers and counter-offers from both sides), the chat ends on a proposal, counter-offer or stated lowest price that the other side neither accepts nor refuses.
criteria.unanswered_opening_offer: The chat ends right after the first price proposal of the negotiation (usually the buyer's opening offer), with no counter-offer or reply.
criteria.walked_away: One party explicitly refuses the other's final offer, says they cannot agree, or leaves the negotiation.
criteria.no_price_talk: The conversation stops early, after greetings or questions about the item, before any price was proposed.
criteria.broken_chat: The chat is confused or broken and never recovers: the parties talk about different items, mix up roles, or complain about the task or website instead of negotiating.
